locations.name: Mandurah
locations.depot: a Fremantle depot, trucked south down the Kwinana Freeway to the Peel
locations.leadTime: What the Fremantle depot is holding, then a straight freeway run south
locations.truck: Tilt-tray for 10ft and 20ft; crane truck where a canal house leaves no side access, and for most 40ft work
locations.metaDesc: Shipping containers for sale and hire in Mandurah and the Peel. Canal blocks, estuary ground and Pinjarra farm drops planned properly. 1300 467 776.
locations.line: Mandurah is a town arranged around water, and most delivery questions here come back to it. The estuary, the Peel Inlet and the Harvey behind it, and the kilometres of canal frontage cut through Halls Head, Port Mandurah and Dawesville mean a great many local blocks were made rather than found: sand pumped out of a channel, shaped, walled off and built on. Made ground behaves differently from a dune that has sat undisturbed for thousands of years, and knowing that before a truck backs down a driveway toward a canal wall saves a lot of grief.
locations.uses: crab pots, rods, outboards and trailer gear for households who ran out of room beside the boat pen years ago, site stores on the builds going up through Lakelands, Madora Bay and Meadow Springs, trade and plant storage on the light industrial land at Greenfields and out at the Peel Business Park in Nambeelup, lock-up for contractors who work at the alumina refinery near Pinjarra or drive up to the Boddington gold mine, furniture held while a canal house is renovated or put on the market, and feed, tack and machinery kept dry on the small rural lots through Stake Hill, Keysbrook and Serpentine
access: Picture a typical canal house in Mandurah and you can picture the delivery problem. The lot is long and narrow, the house fills most of it, the garage takes the street frontage, and everything worth having is out the back facing the water. There is rarely a side path wide enough to walk a wheelie bin down, let alone reverse a tilt-tray. So the realistic spots are the driveway apron, a front setback, or the rear yard reached by crane over the roof, and each of those comes with its own catch. A container parked across the garage apron blocks the garage. The front setback on many estates is governed by design guidelines that frown on anything resembling a shed. A lift over the house needs clear air above it, which means checking the service line to the house, the neighbours' roof lines and anything tied up at the jetty below. None of that rules a container out. It just decides the size, and on a lot of Mandurah canal blocks a 10ft placed well beats a 20ft forced in. The cul-de-sacs at the end of each canal finger are the other pinch point. Their turning heads were drawn for cars and a boat trailer, not a rigid truck with a six metre load, so a driver may need to reverse in from the last intersection. Parked cars, bins on collection day and a boat on a trailer outside number twelve all matter more here than they would in an ordinary street. Away from the water, the older parts of town around the foreshore have shorter, busier streets, and the newer estates east of the freeway at Lakelands and Meadow Springs are wide and straightforward. Out toward Pinjarra and the Yunderups it becomes rural driving again, with gravel shoulders, table drains and gateways built for a tractor.

sections.h: Canal blocks and the wall at the bottom of the garden
p: Every canal lot in Mandurah finishes at a revetment or retaining wall that holds the land up against the water. That wall was engineered to carry a house, a lawn and people walking about. It was not engineered on the assumption that somebody would stand two or three tonnes of steel, plus whatever gets packed inside it, a metre back from the edge. Load placed near the top of a wall pushes sideways on it, and the fill behind these walls is often sand dredged from the channel itself, which is not the most forgiving material. The honest advice is simple: keep a container well back from the waterline, and if the only space available is near the wall, ask the estate manager or an engineer before you order rather than after. We would sooner sell you a smaller box in the right place than a bigger one in the wrong one.

Boat owners are the most common canal buyers, and the reason is usually a crowded garage. Outboards, fuel, crab pots, life jackets and fishing gear smell of salt and bait, they drip, and nobody wants them in the house. A container works well for that job with two provisos. First, rinse and dry gear before it goes in, because wet pots and damp ropes shut inside a steel box on a warm afternoon make a very particular smell and a lot of condensation. Second, give it ventilation. Standard vents are a start and a pair at each end is better. Keep fuel containers to what you genuinely need, keep them upright and away from anything that sparks, and treat the container as a store rather than a workshop.

sections.h: Made ground, winter water and the low side of the estuary
p: Much of residential Mandurah sits only a little above the water it looks out on, and the groundwater underneath rises and falls with the seasons. Through a dry summer a sandy lot at Coodanup, Furnissdale or the lower parts of Halls Head feels firm underfoot. Late in a wet winter the water table can sit close enough to the surface that the same lawn goes spongy, and a loaded rear axle will find the soft patch by sinking into it. If your block has a corner where puddles linger after rain, tell us where it is. That corner is not where a truck should stand and it is not where a container should sit either.

Setting up on made ground is about spreading the weight and keeping the floor dry. Solid pads or treated sleepers under each corner, bedded until they stop moving, and enough height to keep the underside of the floor clear of damp sand and let air pass beneath. On the lowest estuary lots it is worth thinking about where water goes when a winter storm lines up with a big tide and pushes the estuary higher than usual. A container keeps rain off from above and nothing more. Once the estuary is lapping at the doors, the rubber seals are no barrier at all, and a box with nothing in it is buoyant enough to shift off its pads. Put it on the highest practical part of the lot, keep valuable items off the floor on pallets, and do not treat it as a way of keeping anything safe from rising water.

sections.h: Pinjarra, the Yunderups and up into the forest
p: Plenty of Peel deliveries never touch a canal. East of the freeway the country opens onto the Murray and Serpentine flats around Pinjarra, Ravenswood and Barragup, where the soils are heavier and paddocks that are hard in March hold water for weeks in August. Hobby farms, horse properties and turf and vegetable growers all use containers for feed, fencing gear, pumps and machinery. What matters on those jobs is the entry from the road: the culvert under the gateway, the width between the posts, and whether a loaded truck can turn around at the far end rather than reversing a long gravel drive. North and South Yunderup add their own twist, with river canals and narrow residential streets on the Murray that behave more like a canal estate than a farm.

Further east the Darling Scarp rises into jarrah forest around Dwellingup, and a delivery up there is a hill job. Roads narrow, bends tighten, the verge drops away and branches reach across the road. Send photos of the approach and the gate, and be realistic about length: a 20ft is usually the upper limit on a forest block. For contractors heading on to Boddington or the refinery, the site will have its own access rules, inductions and preferred drop point, and we need those details early. A call to 1300 467 776 with the Peel address and the purpose gets you a single price covering the container and getting it there.

faqs.q: Can a container go in the back yard of a Mandurah canal house?
faqs.a: Sometimes, usually by crane over the house rather than through a side gate, because most canal lots have no side access a truck can use. Whether a lift works depends on clear air above the roof, the power line into the house, the neighbours and what is moored below. The other question is the canal wall. Keep a container well back from the water, and if space near the wall is the only option, ask your estate manager or an engineer first. A 10ft in the right spot is often the better buy.

faqs.q: Do I need approval from the City of Mandurah or my estate?
faqs.a: Check with both before you order. The City of Mandurah sets the rules on outbuildings and on how long a container can sit on a residential lot, and many canal and newer estates also carry their own design guidelines about what can be seen from the street or the water. Those rules differ between estates and change over time, so we will not guess at them for you. A short call to the council and a look at your estate guidelines settles it, and it is far easier before delivery than after.

faqs.q: Where does a Mandurah container come from, and can I look at it?
faqs.a: Stock for the Peel is held at a Fremantle depot and trucked south on the freeway. It is a working depot rather than a showroom, so inspection is by arrangement: ring first and a time is organised with the unit you want pulled out where you can open it. If a drive north is not worth it, ask for photos of the actual container on request and they come through before delivery, showing the doors, the floor, the roof and the corners.

faqs.q: Will my boat and fishing gear be all right stored in a container near the estuary?
faqs.a: Yes, if you manage the moisture. Rinse salt off, let pots, ropes and wetsuits dry before they go in, and fit vents so air moves through the box, ideally at both ends. Keep things off the floor on shelving or pallets. Store only the fuel you need, upright and sealed. A container shut up with wet gear on a warm day sweats and smells, and one that breathes stays pleasant to open for years.

locations.name: Rockingham
locations.depot: a Fremantle depot, trucked a short way down the coast past Cockburn Sound
locations.leadTime: Fremantle depot stock, plus any plant or base access paperwork
locations.truck: Tilt-tray for 10ft and 20ft into the beach suburbs and Baldivis; side loader or crane truck for plant sites, lay-down yards and 40ft
locations.metaDesc: Shipping containers for sale and hire in Rockingham, Kwinana and Baldivis. Plant gates, shutdowns, Garden Island and new estates planned right.
locations.line: Rockingham sits beside two very different worlds. Along the coast is a city of beach suburbs stretching from Point Peron down past Safety Bay and Warnbro to Secret Harbour. Running north up the shore of Cockburn Sound into Kwinana is the heaviest industrial strip in Western Australia, with refineries, chemical and fertiliser works, bulk jetties and fabrication shops, and across the water the naval base on Garden Island. A container going to a backyard in Waikiki and one going through a plant gate at Kwinana Beach are entirely different jobs, and knowing which one yours is at the first call saves everybody time.
locations.uses: consumables, tooling and spares staged for shutdowns at the Kwinana refineries, chemical and fertiliser plants, lay-down storage around the East Rockingham and Naval Base industrial land, gear for the marine and fabrication businesses working around Cockburn Sound, contractor lock-up on defence works where the Garden Island site allows it, site stores on the estates filling in Baldivis, Karnup and Wellard, fertiliser, irrigation and machinery storage for the turf and market garden growers on the Baldivis flats, and boat, dive and fishing gear for households at Safety Bay, Shoalwater and Waikiki
access: Three quite different sorts of address make up a Rockingham order book, and each gets planned its own way. The industrial strip runs on permits. Most plants in the Kwinana Industrial Area control who enters, where vehicles may travel, and what can happen inside their operating areas, and a delivery that turns up without the paperwork in place simply waits at the gate. Some sites want the truck to stop at a designated lay-down yard outside the process area and move the container the rest of the way with their own crane or forklift. That is sensible and usually quicker, but it changes which truck we send, so we need to know. The general industrial land at East Rockingham and Naval Base is easier, with broad roads, sealed hardstand and room to stand a truck square to the gate, and a 40ft is a normal request there. The residential side splits in two. The older beach suburbs from Rockingham Beach through Safety Bay and Shoalwater have established gardens, mature trees across the verge, and plenty of blocks where the only way into the back is a narrow side path. Baldivis, Karnup and the estates behind Warnbro are newer, with smaller lots, tight frontages and streets that fill with builders' utes during the day. There, the question is usually where on the lot a container can sit without blocking the garage or annoying the estate guidelines. Wherever you are, three photos help most: the street looking in, the path the truck would take, and the exact spot.

sections.h: Getting through a plant gate at Kwinana
p: Shutdown storage is the bread and butter of Kwinana container work. Contractors want spares, tooling and consumables locked up on site before the first shift, and the containers want to be there before the scaffold goes up, not squeezed in during mobilisation. What slows those jobs down is almost never the container itself. It is the gap between a purchase order raised by a contractor and the site's own access process. Before we book a truck we need the site contact who will meet it, the gate the driver should present at and when that gate is manned, induction or escort requirements, the PPE the site expects, and where exactly the unit is going. If the site prefers to offload it, tell us what lifting gear it has so the right vehicle turns up.

Plenty of plants also care about what they are receiving. Some want a clean floor and doors that open freely, some want the data plate visible, and some will only accept a unit fit for dangerous goods if chemicals or gas cylinders are going inside. That last point matters: a general purpose container is not a dangerous goods store, and if the contents need one, the site's safety team will say so. Ask for photos of the actual unit on request and we will send them before delivery so your site coordinator can see what is coming. Tell us the shutdown window when you enquire, and order as far ahead of it as the job allows.

sections.h: Garden Island, HMAS Stirling and defence work
p: Garden Island sits just off Point Peron and is home to HMAS Stirling, the navy's west coast base. It is reached by a causeway that is not open to general traffic, and nothing goes across it without being arranged through the base. Containers do go there, mostly for contractors carrying out works on the island, but the arrangements belong to the contractor or the defence contact, not to us. Typically that means supplying the driver and vehicle details ahead of time, agreeing an entry time, and having someone meet the truck and escort it to the drop point.

If you are organising a delivery for a defence job, give us the name of whoever manages site access and let them tell us what they need. We would rather ask a few extra questions than have a truck turned around at the causeway. The same patience applies on the water side of Rockingham: the marine businesses around Cockburn Sound frequently work inside secured port or boatyard areas where vehicles need approval, and a quick call to whoever runs the gate saves a wasted trip.

sections.h: Beach ridges, damp swales and Baldivis fill
p: The ground under Rockingham tells a story if you drive across it slowly. The coast here grew seaward over thousands of years as a series of old beach ridges, and between each low ridge lies a swale that sits closer to the water table. That is why Lake Richmond, Lake Cooloongup and Lake Walyungup are there, and it is why two houses in the same street can have very different winters. A block on a ridge drains quickly and stays firm. A block in a swale can stay soft late into spring, and the patch of lawn that squelches underfoot is the patch a truck will sink into. Mention it at the quote and we will plan around it.

Baldivis is different again. Much of it was paddocks, turf and vegetable farms not long ago, and the new estates were built up with imported fill before the houses went on. That fill has usually been compacted for the slab but not necessarily for the back corner of the lot where you want a container. Put solid pads or sleepers under all four corners, check them against each other with a level before the box comes off the truck, and keep the floor lifted clear of the ground. Further east toward the Serpentine River the land flattens and holds water through winter, so rural drops out that way are best booked when the paddock has had a chance to dry.

The southern end of the city is dune country. Secret Harbour, Golden Bay and Singleton back onto tall, vegetated coastal dunes, and some lots are cut into their flanks with loose white sand on the high side. Loose sand will not hold an edge or a corner, so a container dropped on the uphill side of one of those lots can creep over a few winters as the sand beneath it slowly shifts. Set it on the flattest, most settled ground on the block, keep it back from any batter, and plant or mulch the bare sand around it so the wind has nothing to strip away.

faqs.q: Can you deliver inside the Kwinana Industrial Area?
faqs.a: Yes, regularly, but the site sets the terms. We need a site contact, the gate the truck should present at and when it is manned, any induction or escort needed, and where the unit is going. Some plants would rather take the container at a lay-down yard and move it inside with their own gear, which is fine and often quicker. Tell us the shutdown or project date at the enquiry so the unit can be organised well ahead of it.

faqs.q: Can a container be delivered onto Garden Island?
faqs.a: Only when the delivery has been arranged through the base. The causeway is not open to general traffic, so the contractor or defence contact running the work organises access, usually with vehicle and driver details supplied in advance and someone meeting the truck. Put us in touch with whoever manages site access and we will give them what they ask for. We cannot simply turn up at the causeway, and nobody should expect that.

faqs.q: I have a new lot in Baldivis. What should I know before ordering?
faqs.a: Three things. Check the City of Rockingham rules and your estate design guidelines, because some estates restrict what can sit in view of the street and for how long. Look at the ground where the container will go: new estates are built on imported fill that is compacted under the slab but not always in the back corner. And measure the frontage, because smaller lots often leave only the driveway, and a 20ft there blocks the garage. Send photos and we will suggest the size that fits.

faqs.q: Is it better to hire or buy for a Kwinana shutdown?
faqs.a: For a single shutdown with a clear finish date, hire usually makes more sense. You avoid owning a steel box once the crew has moved on, and collection is arranged at the end. If the same site runs shutdowns every year, or you want permanent storage for a maintenance crew, buying tends to win after a couple of seasons. Tell us how long the job runs and how often it repeats, and we will price both options side by side.

faqs.q: Will a container rust quickly at Safety Bay or Shoalwater?
faqs.a: Not if it is looked after. Containers are built to cross oceans on an open deck, so salt in the air is nothing new to them. What shortens their life near Cockburn Sound is leaf litter and sand piling on the roof, the underside sitting on damp ground, and scrapes left bare until they turn orange. Keep the roof clear, get the floor off the ground on pads, touch up bare metal with a decent primer, and grease the door hinges and locking bars now and then. That is most of the maintenance a coastal container needs.

locations.name: Joondalup
locations.depot: a Fremantle depot, trucked north up the Mitchell Freeway to the northern suburbs
locations.leadTime: Fremantle depot stock, then a freeway run up the northern corridor
locations.truck: Tilt-tray for 10ft and 20ft on most lots; crane truck for laneway lots, tall retaining walls and 40ft
locations.metaDesc: Shipping containers for sale and hire in Joondalup, Wanneroo and the northern corridor up to Yanchep. Building sites, small lots and Wangara units.
locations.line: North of Joondalup the coast has been turning into suburbs for decades, and it has not stopped. Clarkson, Butler, Alkimos, Eglinton, Yanchep and Two Rocks now run in a near-continuous strip beside Marmion Avenue, with the freeway and the railway extended north to keep pace. A great deal of container work in the corridor follows the builders: a box dropped on a vacant lot to hold tools and fittings while a house goes up, then collected once the keys are handed over. The rest is split between the established suburbs around the Joondalup city centre, the industrial areas at Wangara and Neerabup, and the growers inland along Wanneroo Road.
locations.uses: owner-builder and trade site storage on the house lots at Alkimos, Eglinton, Yanchep and Two Rocks, stock and equipment for the businesses packed into the Wangara, Landsdale and Neerabup industrial areas, packing and machinery storage on the vegetable and strawberry farms through Carabooda, Nowergup and Mariginiup, gear for sporting clubs and schools across both council areas, household storage while an older home in Duncraig, Kingsley or Woodvale is extended, furniture held during a move, and boats and fishing gear for people who launch at Hillarys or Ocean Reef
access: The northern corridor has two shapes of residential block and they make for very different deliveries. Established suburbs around Joondalup, such as Edgewater, Heathridge, Craigie and Mullaloo, have lots that were drawn for a quarter-acre life: a driveway down one side, a gate to the back, and usually room for a 20ft on a tilt-tray if the verge trees cooperate. The newer estates are tighter. Lots at Alkimos, Eglinton, Butler and Banksia Grove are often narrow and deep, the house is built close to both side boundaries, and a good share of them are laneway lots with the garage at the back off a narrow rear lane and only a front garden onto the street. On a laneway lot the lane is often the only way in, and lanes were not drawn with a rigid truck in mind, so we need a photo looking down it and a note of anything parked there. Building sites add their own rules. The builder controls the lot until handover, the crossover and footpath may not be finished, and there may be a skip, a scaffold and a pallet of bricks exactly where you pictured the container. Ask your site supervisor where it may go before you book. Wangara is the other access puzzle: a lot of it is strata industrial units that share a narrow common driveway, so a delivery can block neighbours unless it is timed with the body corporate or the adjoining tenants. Neerabup lots are larger and easier. Out along Wanneroo Road, farm tracks are sandy and a loaded truck needs a firm route to the shed.

sections.h: A container on the lot while the house goes up
p: Owner-builders and trades like a lockable box on site for the same reasons: tools stay there overnight, deliveries of fittings have somewhere to go, and nobody spends the first hour of every day unloading a ute. On a building site, though, a container is a guest. The builder decides where it goes, and it needs to be somewhere that will not interfere with the slab, the frame, the scaffold, the brick drops or the concrete pump. The front corner of a lot is often the obvious spot, but that is also where the crossover, the meter box and the services come in. A short conversation with the supervisor about sequence saves moving it halfway through the build.

Hire suits most of these jobs because the need has a natural end at practical completion. When the house is finished the container comes off the lot before landscaping starts, and you never have to find space for it again. Buying makes sense if the plan is to keep it afterwards as a garden store or workshop, and in that case think about where it will finally live on the finished lot rather than where it is handy during construction, because moving it later is another delivery. Whichever you choose, check the City of Wanneroo or City of Joondalup rules for your address, along with the estate guidelines, before the unit arrives.

Security is the other reason people put a container on a building site. Tools, copper, appliances and fittings left in a half-built house are an easy target, and new estates with streets of empty frames attract exactly that attention. A container with a lockbox over the padlock is a much harder proposition than a garage without a door. Position it where neighbours and passing traffic can see the doors rather than tucked away behind the frame, and keep the key with whoever arrives first each morning. Photos of the actual unit on request before delivery show you the condition of the doors and seals so there are no surprises.

sections.h: Retaining walls and cut limestone
p: The coastal ridges running up to Yanchep are limestone, and developers level them by cutting the high ground and filling the low. The result is a landscape of stepped lots held apart by retaining walls, some of them surprisingly tall, and a lot of back gardens where hard caprock sits just under a skim of sand. Caprock is excellent to stand a container on once the corners are packed level, although it is rarely flat and digging into it is slow. What deserves more thought is the retaining wall. Walls on the upper side of a lot are built to hold back what is behind them. They were not designed for an extra point load sitting near the top. Keep a container back from the edge of any wall, and if the only space is near one, ask whoever built it.

Tall walls also shape how a truck can work. A tilt-tray needs to back up to the drop spot on firm ground, and on a stepped lot that spot may be a metre above or below the driveway. A crane truck reaching over from the street may be the only sensible way in, and it needs enough clear air above the lot to swing the load. Overhead power is usually underground in the new estates, which helps, but street trees and neighbouring roofs still count. Photos from the street and from the spot back toward the street tell us most of it.

sections.h: Wangara, Neerabup and the growers east of Wanneroo Road
p: Wangara is one of the busiest light industrial areas in Perth, and it shows. Trades, wholesalers and manufacturers are packed into strata units with shared driveways and roller doors facing each other across a narrow common area. A container can sit neatly on a unit's parking bay or in a corner of the common property, but only with the body corporate's agreement, and the delivery itself briefly blocks the driveway for everyone. Timing it early in the day and letting the neighbours know avoids most of the friction. Neerabup to the north has larger lots and wider roads and is simpler, and Landsdale sits between the two in character.

Inland, the market gardens and orchards of Carabooda, Nowergup and Mariginiup have long used containers for crates, irrigation parts, fertiliser and machinery. Farm deliveries here are about the track: soft, sandy tracks between beds can bog a loaded truck even in summer, so we need a firm route from the road to the drop point, with any turning space noted. Growers keeping sprays or fertiliser should look up the storage rules before anything else, since an ordinary dry-freight box does not meet them just by having a lock. Phone 1300 467 776, say which suburb and what the box will hold, and the price you get back already includes the truck.

faqs.q: Can I keep a container on my lot while my house is being built?
faqs.a: Usually, yes, as long as the builder agrees on where it goes. On a building site the builder controls the lot until handover, and the container has to stay clear of the slab, scaffold, pump and brick drops. Check the City of Wanneroo or City of Joondalup rules and your estate guidelines too. Hire suits most builds because the box leaves at completion, before the landscaping goes in.

faqs.q: Will a 20ft fit on a laneway lot at Alkimos or Butler?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but the laneway usually decides it rather than the lot. Rear lanes are narrow, often have cars and bins in them, and a rigid truck needs to be able to line up square and get back out. Send a photo looking down the lane from each end, one of the spot, and the width of the gap you have available. On a tight laneway lot a 10ft is often the practical answer, or a crane lift from the street.

faqs.q: Can you deliver into a strata unit complex at Wangara?
faqs.a: Yes, with a bit of planning. Check with your body corporate before a container goes on common property or a parking bay, and let the neighbouring tenants know because the truck briefly blocks the shared driveway. An early delivery is kindest to everyone. Send us a photo of the driveway and the spot, and we will tell you which truck suits.

faqs.q: Which council do I check with in the northern suburbs?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. The City of Joondalup covers the established suburbs from Duncraig and Hillarys up to Burns Beach and Iluka. The City of Wanneroo covers Wanneroo itself, the industrial areas at Wangara and Neerabup, and the corridor north from Clarkson and Mindarie to Two Rocks. Each has its own rules on containers and outbuildings, so confirm with the right one before ordering.

faqs.q: Do you deliver as far north as Two Rocks and Gingin?
faqs.a: Yes. Yanchep and Two Rocks are part of the same run up the corridor, and rural lots further out toward Gingin and the Shire of Gingin are reachable too, as long as the approach suits a loaded truck. The dunes around Two Rocks are steep and some newer lots sit well above or below the road, so send a photo of the driveway and the spot. For rural lots, tell us about the track from the road and whether there is space to turn around.

locations.name: Busselton
locations.depot: a Fremantle depot, run south past Bunbury onto the Bussell Highway
locations.leadTime: Fremantle depot stock, holiday traffic on the cape and winter ground
locations.truck: Tilt-tray for 10ft and 20ft; crane truck for steep cape blocks and tight vineyard sheds, side loader where a 40ft goes to a winery
locations.metaDesc: Shipping containers for sale and hire in Busselton, Dunsborough and Margaret River. Wineries, holiday homes and low Vasse ground handled properly.
locations.line: Busselton sits on low, flat land between the calm water of Geographe Bay and the Vasse wetlands, and the country changes character as you head west. Dunsborough, Eagle Bay and Yallingup climb onto the granite and limestone of the cape, then Caves Road runs south through vineyards and forest to Margaret River. Container work down here is a mix no other part of the state quite matches: winery sheds, holiday houses whose owners live in Perth, new estates at Vasse and Yalyalup, surf and boat gear, and cattle and dairy country behind the coast. Each needs a slightly different conversation.
locations.uses: barrel, bin and equipment storage at the wineries and vineyards from Yallingup down through Wilyabrup and Cowaramup to Margaret River, linen and maintenance gear for holiday rental managers, boats, kayaks and surfboards for households in Dunsborough, Quindalup and Eagle Bay, site stores on the estates growing through Vasse, Yalyalup and Dunsborough Lakes, staging and equipment for events between seasons, hay, fencing and machinery on the beef and dairy country inland toward Carbunup and Metricup, and stock and packaging for the breweries and distilleries along Caves Road
access: Town and cape are two different delivery landscapes. Busselton itself is flat, with generous streets and older lots in West Busselton, Broadwater and Abbey that usually have space down one side. The newer estates at Vasse, Yalyalup and Provence are laid out for cars and trailers and are generally easy for a tilt-tray. The cape is harder. Around Dunsborough, Eagle Bay and Yallingup, many lots are steep, rocky and heavily treed with peppermint, marri and banksia, and the roads are narrow with little shoulder. Driveways can drop sharply off the road or bend between granite boulders, and a container that can be placed on a flat site in town may need a crane on the cape. Caves Road is the main artery south and it is busy. During school holidays, around Christmas and at Easter it fills with caravans, cyclists and visitors looking at the view instead of the road, so deliveries are best booked outside the peak. Wineries and farms have their own rhythm: gravel tracks, vineyard rows, fruit bins stacked in the yard, and gates that need to be left as found. Around Margaret River the forest closes in, especially through the tall karri stands to the south, and overhanging branches decide how high a load can travel. Whatever the address, a photo from the road, one along the drive and one of the spot usually answers every question before a truck leaves Fremantle.

sections.h: Low ground between the bay and the Vasse
p: Much of Busselton sits only a few metres above sea level, with the Vasse River, the Lower Vasse and the Vasse-Wonnerup wetlands at its back and the bay at its front. In summer that makes very little difference. Through a wet winter the water table comes up under the sandy ground, low corners of lots stay wet for weeks, and the lawn that looked firm in February will not take a loaded truck in August. If your block is near the wetlands or in one of the lower streets, tell us where the water sits after rain, because that is where the truck should not go and where the container should not be placed.

The setup that suits this ground is pads or sleepers under each corner, levelled against one another and set on the firmest part of the lot, with the floor kept clear of the sand so it can dry out. On the lowest land it is worth thinking about storms as well. When a winter front pushes water into the bay on a big tide, the lowest parts of town can see water where it is not usually found. A container keeps rain off from above but it does nothing to keep rising water out. Seawater pushed up through the town will find its way around door gaskets, and a light, empty unit can be floated clear of where you left it. Put it on the high side of the block and keep anything that matters up off the floor.

Inland, the beef and dairy country toward Carbunup, Metricup and Jindong tells the same story on a larger scale. Paddocks that carry a truck easily through summer turn heavy and wet after the winter rains, and gateways churned by stock and tractors are the softest ground on the farm. Farm drops are best planned for when the ground is dry, or onto a gravel pad near the sheds where a loader can move the container later. Tell us the width of the gateway at its narrowest point, whether there is a grid or culvert on the way in, and where a loaded truck can turn around.

sections.h: Wineries, vintage and what a steel box does to wine
p: Wineries and vineyards through Wilyabrup, Yallingup and Margaret River use containers for barrels, dry goods, packaging, irrigation parts, tractors and spare equipment. The one thing to plan around is vintage, which usually runs late summer into autumn. For those weeks every road into a vineyard is full of harvesters, bin trailers and trucks carrying fruit, and nobody has spare time to meet a container delivery. Get it in before vintage starts, or after the last fruit is in, and make sure the drop point will not be in the way of the fruit coming in.

Temperature is the other issue for anyone storing wine or anything temperature sensitive. A standard steel container in full sun gets hot inside on a summer afternoon, and it swings more than a well-insulated building would. That is fine for tanks, hoses, tools and packaging. It is not fine for bottled stock or barrels holding wine. For those, ask about an insulated or refrigerated unit, or at least site the container in shade with good ventilation. A light roof colour helps a little. Tell us what is going in and we will match the container to it rather than leave you to find out in February.

sections.h: Holiday houses and owners who live somewhere else
p: A lot of homes on the cape are holiday houses and rentals whose owners live in Perth or further away. Those deliveries work smoothly when the details are settled in advance, and go wrong when the driver arrives at a locked gate with nobody answering the phone. We need a contact who can answer on the day, the gate code or key arrangement, a note on whether any dogs are on the property, and a photo of the exact spot with something in the picture that marks the corner. If a property manager looks after the house, put us in touch with them. If a neighbour will be there, that works too.

It is also worth checking what the local rules allow before a container lands on a holiday lot. The City of Busselton covers Busselton, Dunsborough and Yallingup, while Margaret River, Cowaramup and Augusta fall under the Shire of Augusta-Margaret River. Each has its own view on containers in residential and rural areas, and strata or estate rules can add more. A short call before ordering avoids a letter later. Call 1300 467 776 with the holiday address and what you need stored; the quote you receive covers both the box and the trip down from Fremantle.

Holiday rentals have their own uses for a container. Managers use them to hold spare linen, outdoor furniture, cleaning gear and the barbecue that has to vanish before guests arrive, while owners use them to lock away the boat, the surfboards and the car trailer when the house is let out. A lockable box separate from the house means a family's belongings stay out of reach of guests without a room being shut off. Site it where guests will not reverse into it, and where it will not spoil the view that someone is paying to look at.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to a winery during vintage?
faqs.a: We can, but it is rarely the best plan. During vintage every vineyard track is busy with harvesters, bin trailers and fruit trucks, and a container delivery gets in the way. Booking before vintage starts or after the last fruit is in makes everyone's life easier. If it must happen mid-vintage, give us a contact who can direct the driver and a drop point well clear of where the fruit comes in.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to my Dunsborough holiday house while I am in Perth?
faqs.a: Yes. We need someone we can reach on the day, the gate code or key arrangements, whether there are dogs on the property, and a photo of the exact spot with something that marks it clearly. A property manager or a neighbour on site makes it easier still. If the block is steep or heavily treed, send a photo along the driveway as well so we can decide between a tilt-tray and a crane truck.

faqs.q: Is Margaret River covered by the City of Busselton?
faqs.a: No. Busselton, Dunsborough, Yallingup and Vasse are in the City of Busselton, while Margaret River, Cowaramup, Witchcliffe and Augusta are in the Shire of Augusta-Margaret River. Each has its own rules on containers in residential and rural zones, so check with the right one for your address before you order. We deliver to both.

faqs.q: Can I store wine in a shipping container?
faqs.a: Not in a standard one left in the sun. A plain steel container heats up quickly on a summer afternoon and cools overnight, and that swing is hard on bottled wine and barrels. For wine, ask about an insulated or refrigerated container. For tools, tanks, packaging and machinery a standard unit is fine, especially if it is shaded and ventilated. Tell us what is going in when you enquire.

faqs.q: Can a container go on a steep block at Eagle Bay or Yallingup?
faqs.a: Often, yes, but it usually needs a crane truck rather than a tilt-tray. Cape blocks tend to fall away from the road with granite, peppermints and banksia in the way, and a tilt-tray needs a straight, firm run to the spot. A crane truck can reach over from the road if there is clear air above the lot. Send photos of the road, the drive and the spot, and mention any overhead power so we can tell you what will work.

locations.name: Albany
locations.depot: a Fremantle depot, carted the full length of the Albany Highway to the south coast
locations.leadTime: Fremantle depot stock and a truck heading down the Albany Highway
locations.truck: Tilt-tray for 10ft and 20ft on firm approaches; crane truck for the steep streets under Mount Clarence and Mount Melville, and for 40ft
locations.metaDesc: Shipping containers for sale and hire in Albany and the Great Southern. Damp-climate advice, granite blocks and farm drops around harvest and seeding.
locations.line: Albany sits at the far end of the Albany Highway, on a coast that takes the weather straight off the Southern Ocean. Cold fronts roll through from the south-west, the drizzle can last for days, and even in summer the air off King George Sound carries more moisture than Perth ever sees. That climate, more than distance, shapes how a container should be chosen and set up here. Get the ventilation and the siting right, and a steel box is one of the most useful things on a Great Southern property. Get it wrong, and you open the doors in August to find mould on everything you cared about.
locations.uses: equipment, fuel and chemical storage for the blue gum plantation and harvest contractors, grain, seed and machinery storage on the cropping and sheep properties through Narrikup, Kendenup and out toward the Stirling Range, gear for the vineyards around Mount Barker, the Porongurups and Denmark, trade and stock storage on the Milpara and Mirambeena industrial land, pots, nets and boat gear for people who fish out of Emu Point and Princess Royal Harbour, site stores on the builds at Bayonet Head, McKail and Little Grove, and furniture held while an older weatherboard in Middleton Beach or Mount Melville is restumped or extended
access: Albany is built around granite. Mount Clarence and Mount Melville rise straight behind the town centre, Mount Adelaide sits over the harbour, and the older streets climb their slopes at gradients that would make most drivers change down twice. Streets in the older parts of town, from Stirling Terrace up toward the lookouts and across into the Middleton Beach side, are narrow and steep, with stone walls on the boundary, established trees over the road and driveways that tip sharply up or down from the kerb. A tilt-tray bed can ground out on a steep crossover before the container is anywhere near the spot, and on some of those blocks a crane truck reaching from the street is the only sensible option. The newer suburbs east and north, at Bayonet Head, McKail, Yakamia and Lange, are much gentler, with wider roads and more room. The industrial land around Milpara and the Mirambeena area is easier still, flat and built for heavy vehicles. Ground varies block to block. Weathered granite and gravel on the rises carry a container well, but grey sands on the flats hold water through winter, and the swampy country around Lake Seppings and the creek lines stays soft for months. Farm and plantation access depends on the season: gravel roads corrugate in summer and soften through winter, paddock gateways get churned, and log trucks share the plantation tracks with everyone else. Photos of the street, the approach and the spot, plus a note on which way the block slopes, tell us most of what we need.

sections.h: Damp as a way of life
p: Albany gets more rain than Perth, but what matters more for a container is that it is damp. Rain falls on a lot of days rather than all at once, cloud and drizzle hang about for most of winter, and the nights are cool enough that moisture in the air condenses on anything cold. The inside face of a steel roof is exactly that. On a still winter night, warm moist air trapped in a container gives up its water on the underside of the roof, and it drips back down onto whatever is stored below. Furniture, mattresses, cardboard boxes, books and clothing all suffer, and they suffer slowly enough that nobody notices until the damage is done.

The fixes are not complicated but they need doing from the start. Ventilation is the most important: vents at both ends so air passes through, and whirlybirds if the contents matter. Nothing damp should go in, and anything absorbent should be wrapped or boxed in plastic and kept up off the floor on pallets. A moisture absorber or two helps in a container that stays shut for long stretches. Face the doors away from the prevailing south-westerly so rain is not driven straight at the seals, and keep leaves and twigs off the roof so water runs away instead of pooling. Ask about the grade too, because only cargo-worthy and new single-trip units are sold as wind and watertight.

sections.h: Granite, gravel and the long run south
p: Granite is a gift and a nuisance. Where bare rock sits at or near the surface it is about the best ground in the country for carrying a container, because nothing under it is going to settle. The trouble is that granite is rarely level and it is slippery when wet, so getting four corners to the same height takes packing rather than digging, and a truck working on sloping rock after rain needs care. If your spot is on rock, say so, and we will bring enough timber to pack the low side up rather than turning up expecting a flat gravel pad.

Distance is the other thing to plan for. Everything comes down the Albany Highway through Williams, Kojonup and Mount Barker, and a container that goes the wrong way is expensive to put right. So be clear about what you need from the start: the length, whether you want a standard height or a high cube, which way the doors should face once it is placed, and whether a personnel door, extra vents or a shelving fit-out should be done before it leaves. If you are likely to need a second container in the next few months, mention it now so both can travel on the same truck. Talk to us on 1300 467 776 about the Great Southern address and the job, and the figure you hear includes the long haul south.

Older homes add another reason to hire. Many weatherboard and brick houses in the established parts of Albany are being restumped, reroofed, extended or refitted, and the contents have to go somewhere while the work happens. A container on the front lawn or the driveway keeps furniture close, locked and dry, provided it is set up properly for the climate, and it leaves once the builders do. If the job is a restump, place the container where it will not block the trades working under the house, and leave room for the timber and steel deliveries that will follow.

sections.h: Harvest, seeding and plantation work
p: Great Southern farms keep a calendar that deliveries should respect. Seeding runs through autumn into early winter, lambing follows, and harvest for grain and canola usually starts in late spring and runs into summer. During harvest nobody on a cropping property has time to stand around waiting for a truck, and during the wettest part of winter paddock access can be poor. The easiest windows are usually late summer and early autumn, when the ground is firm and the header has been put away. If a container has to arrive mid-harvest, give us a farm contact who will actually answer the phone and a drop point near the sheds that will not get in the way of the grain trucks.

Plantation work has its own pattern. Blue gum harvest and haulage contractors move between properties, their access tracks are shared with log trucks, and the drop point may be a landing in the middle of a plantation rather than an address with a street number. We need a GPS pin or clear directions from the nearest public road, the site contact, and any induction or access rule the plantation manager sets. Treat the container as a secure store rather than a safe haven in a bushfire: it is not protection for people or contents, so site it on cleared ground away from fuel and keep the area around it slashed.

faqs.q: How do I stop things going mouldy in a container in Albany?
faqs.a: Airflow and keeping things dry at the start. Fit vents at both ends, and whirlybirds if you are storing furniture, clothing or paper. Do not put anything damp inside. Wrap soft items in plastic, keep everything up off the floor on pallets, and use moisture absorbers if the doors stay shut for long periods. Face the doors away from the south-westerly and keep the roof clear of leaves. Albany's damp is steady rather than dramatic, so a well-ventilated container stays dry and a sealed one does not.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to a farm out toward the Stirling Range in winter?
faqs.a: Yes, but the paddock and the gateway will decide how. Through the wettest months gravel roads soften, gateways churned by stock turn to mud, and a loaded truck needs firm ground all the way to the drop point. Often the best answer in winter is dropping the container on a gravel pad near the sheds and letting your loader shift it later. Tell us the road surface, the gateway width and where a truck can turn around, and we will plan it.

faqs.q: Do you deliver to Denmark, Mount Barker and Walpole as well?
faqs.a: Yes. Mount Barker and the Porongurups are on the way in from the highway, and Denmark and Walpole are further west along the South Coast Highway. Council rules differ: the Shire of Plantagenet covers Mount Barker and Kendenup, the Shire of Denmark covers Denmark, and Walpole is in the Shire of Manjimup. Check with the right one before ordering. Around Denmark and Walpole the forest closes in, so send a photo of the driveway so we can check for low branches.

faqs.q: Can I see the container before it is sent to Albany?
faqs.a: Stock for the Great Southern is held at a Fremantle depot, and inspection there is by arrangement rather than a walk-in, so ring first if you happen to be in Perth. For most Albany buyers the better option is photos of the actual container on request, sent before delivery, showing the corners, the door end, the roof and the length of the floor. If anything in the photos is not what you expected, it gets sorted before the container goes on the truck.

faqs.q: Can a container go on a steep block under Mount Clarence or Mount Melville?
faqs.a: Often, but usually by crane rather than tilt-tray. The streets on those slopes are narrow and steep, and a tilt-tray bed can ground out on a sharp crossover before the container reaches the spot. A crane truck standing in the street can lift over a fence or a wall if there is clear air above. Send photos of the street, the driveway and the spot, and tell us about any power lines or trees overhead.

locations.name: Palmerston
locations.depot: a Darwin depot in the Berrimah area, a short run down the highway to Palmerston
locations.leadTime: Darwin depot stock, with build-up storms the main thing that moves a booking
locations.truck: Tilt-tray for 10ft and 20ft on most Palmerston lots; crane truck for townhouse complexes, rear yards and 40ft
locations.metaDesc: Shipping containers for sale and hire in Palmerston NT, supplied from Darwin depot stock. Defence postings, townhouses and Yarrawonga trades covered.
locations.line: Palmerston sits a short run from the depot where our Darwin stock is held, and that closeness changes the shape of a delivery. Stock sits in the Berrimah area, topped up off the wharf at East Arm, and the run out to Palmerston is short and on good roads. So a booking that has to move because of a storm, or a change from a 20ft to a 10ft at the last minute, is a minor rearrangement rather than a problem. The more interesting questions here are about people and paperwork: defence families on postings, rental properties, body corporates, and the new suburbs still taking shape on the eastern edge.
locations.uses: household storage for defence families posting in and out of Robertson Barracks, furniture held between a lease ending and the next one starting, trade and stock storage across the Yarrawonga light industrial area, site stores on the house builds going up through Zuccoli, Johnston and the newer eastern estates, sporting club, school and community group equipment, stock for small retailers around the Palmerston city centre, and boats, camper trailers and fishing gear kept out of the sun between trips to the harbour
access: Palmerston was built as a planned satellite city from the 1980s, and it still reads that way from a truck cab. The older suburbs such as Gray, Driver, Moulden and Woodroffe were laid out around loop roads and cul-de-sacs, with shaded streets and houses set back behind mature gardens. Big trees over the kerb and driveways that run beside the house are the usual constraints there, and most lots can take a 20ft if the truck can line up. Further out, in Rosebery, Bakewell, Durack and Farrar, the blocks are a little tighter and the houses sit closer together. The eastern estates are the newest and change fastest: some streets still have lots waiting to be built on, kerbs and crossovers are not always finished, and the ground beside a finished house can be freshly placed fill. Townhouse and unit complexes are their own category. They often have a gated entry, a narrow internal driveway with speed humps, carports with low roofs, and very little open ground, so a container usually goes in a visitor bay or a common area with the body corporate's agreement, or not at all. Yarrawonga is straightforward, with industrial lots, roller doors, room to turn and hardstand that suits a truck. Ground across Palmerston is mostly laterite gravel that carries weight well once compacted, but freshly filled lots and the lower ground near the creeks and lagoons stay soft through the wet. Photos of the street, the approach and the spot, plus the gate code and any access instructions, let us plan the whole job before the truck leaves the depot.

sections.h: Close to the depot, and why that helps
p: Palmerston buyers have an advantage most of the Territory does not: the stock is just up the road. Inspection at the depot in the Berrimah area is by arrangement, and for someone in Palmerston it is a realistic thing to do rather than a theoretical offer. Ring first so the unit you are interested in is pulled out where you can open the doors, walk the floor and look at the seals. If that does not suit, ask for photos of the actual container on request and they come through before delivery.

Being close also makes rescheduling painless. In the build-up and the wet, an afternoon storm can drop enough rain in half an hour to turn a lawn to mud, and a truck standing on it will leave ruts that take the rest of the season to disappear. Because the run is short, moving a booking to a drier morning is a small rearrangement. The same applies if you change your mind about the size once you have measured again, or if the builder is not ready. The date is confirmed when you place the order, and if anything changes at your end, tell us as early as you can. For businesses in Yarrawonga the same flexibility means a container can be booked around a stocktake, a fit-out or a delivery of their own, rather than the other way round. If you are unsure whether a 10ft or a 20ft suits, measure the space, including the swing of the doors, and send us the numbers with a photo.

sections.h: Postings, rentals and body corporates
p: Palmerston has a large defence community, and postings create a very particular storage need. A family arrives before a house is ready, or leaves a house before the removalist can take everything, or needs somewhere to keep the boat and the camper while living in something smaller for a while. A container on hire covers the gap and goes away when it is no longer needed. If you are on a posting, check what your relocation arrangements already cover before you order, and tell us how long you expect to need it. Hire suits a defined gap; buying suits storage that will go with you to the next property.

Renters and townhouse owners have extra people to ask. A tenant needs the landlord's permission before a container goes on a rental property, and it pays to get that in writing. In a townhouse or unit complex, the body corporate decides whether a container can sit on common property or a visitor bay, and for how long. The City of Palmerston has its own rules for containers on residential land, and whether a container that is staying needs a building permit or an engineered tie-down in this wind region is a question for a building certifier. None of that is a reason not to order, but it should be settled before a truck turns up.

The newer eastern estates bring a different kind of paperwork. Zuccoli, Johnston and the streets beyond them are full of lots under construction, and a container on a building site sits there with the builder's agreement, placed where it will not get in the way of the slab, the frame or the deliveries. Estate guidelines may also say something about outbuildings and what can be seen from the street. On a finished lot, remember that the fill beside a new house has not had many wet seasons to settle, so a container should go on well-bedded pads rather than straight onto new turf.

sections.h: Build-up afternoons and a steel box in the sun
p: From around October the build-up brings heavy, humid heat and afternoon storms with a lot of lightning, then the monsoon arrives and the rain settles in. A steel container sitting in full sun through that season gets very hot inside, and when a storm cools the air suddenly, moisture condenses on the inside of the roof and walls. That is hard on anything with electronics, adhesives or batteries, on paper and fabric, and on furniture that has come up from a drier climate. Ventilation is the first answer, with vents at both ends and whirlybirds if the contents are sensitive. Shade helps a great deal, whether from trees or a shade structure, as long as any structure has the approvals it needs.

Siting matters too. Put the container on the highest practical part of the lot, clear of the path water takes when a storm dumps on the suburb, and on pads rather than directly on the ground so air moves underneath and the underside dries after each downpour. Monsoon rain from above stays outside; stormwater pooling around the base is another matter, because it seeps past the gaskets, and deep enough water can move an unladen unit. Keep the roof clear of leaves and mango litter so water runs off instead of sitting in a corner. Palmerston buyers can call 1300 467 776 with the street and the contents, and the answer is one number, delivery included.

faqs.q: Can I look at a container before it is delivered to Palmerston?
faqs.a: Yes. Our Darwin stock is held at a depot in the Berrimah area, a short drive from Palmerston, and inspection there is by arrangement. Ring first so the unit you want is pulled out where you can open it and look inside properly. If a visit does not suit, ask for photos of the actual container on request and we will send them before delivery, showing the doors, floor, roof and corners.

faqs.q: Can I put a container on a rental property or in a townhouse complex?
faqs.a: Only with the right permission. On a rental you need the landlord's agreement, ideally in writing. In a townhouse or unit complex the body corporate decides whether a container may sit on common property or in a visitor bay, and for how long. Check the City of Palmerston rules as well. Once that is sorted, send photos of the entry, the internal driveway and the spot, because gated complexes often have low carports and tight turns.

faqs.q: Does a container in Palmerston need to be tied down?
faqs.a: It depends on how long it stays and what it is used for. Palmerston is in a cyclone wind region, and a container that becomes a permanent fixture may need a building permit and an engineered tie-down. That is a question for a building certifier and the City of Palmerston, not for us, and it is worth asking before the unit arrives. An empty container is lighter than most people think, so do not assume it will stay put in a big blow.

faqs.q: Is hire or buying better for a defence posting?
faqs.a: Hire usually suits a posting with a known end date, such as a gap between houses or a few months in temporary accommodation. The container goes when you do. Buying makes more sense if you want long-term storage on a property you own, or if the container will go with you. Check what your relocation arrangements already cover, tell us how long you need it for, and we will price both.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to a business in Yarrawonga?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is usually one of the simpler jobs in Palmerston. Yarrawonga lots are built for trucks, with hardstand, wide gates and room to turn. Tell us whether a forklift is on site, where the container should go, and whether anything overhead, such as an awning, a gantry or a power line, will affect a tilt-tray or crane. For a 40ft, a side loader or crane truck is often the better choice, and we will confirm which one fits once we see photos.

locations.name: Humpty Doo
locations.depot: a Darwin depot in the Berrimah area, trucked out the Stuart and Arnhem Highways to the rural area
locations.leadTime: Darwin depot stock, the state of your driveway and the wet season
locations.truck: Tilt-tray for 10ft and 20ft on firm gravel drives; side loader or crane truck for 40ft, packing sheds and anywhere a tilt cannot turn
locations.metaDesc: Shipping containers for sale and hire in Humpty Doo and the Litchfield rural area, from Howard Springs to Berry Springs and Batchelor. 1300 467 776.
locations.line: The rural area south-east of Darwin is where the Top End goes for room. Humpty Doo, Howard Springs, Virginia, Bees Creek, Coolalinga, Berry Springs and the blocks strung along the Arnhem and Stuart Highways are acreage country: woodland, mango orchards, horse paddocks, nurseries and houses set well back from gravel roads. Containers are everywhere out here because a steel box suits the life. What makes a rural delivery work is rarely the container itself. It is the culvert at the front gate, the length of the drive, whether anyone is home, and which month it is.
locations.uses: packing, carton and equipment storage on the mango orchards through Humpty Doo, Lambells Lagoon and Acacia Hills, bore pump and irrigation spares, slashers, mowers and machinery on acreage blocks at Howard Springs, Virginia, Bees Creek and Girraween, feed and tack on horse properties, nursery and market garden stores around Berry Springs and Darwin River, workshop and stock storage for the trades and small businesses around Coolalinga, lock-up at fishing camps out toward the Mary River and Corroboree, and household storage on blocks at Batchelor and the Coomalie district
access: Rural addresses in Litchfield are easy to describe and surprisingly hard to find. Many roads look alike, block numbers are not always posted, and the house can sit hundreds of metres back behind the trees with no sign of it from the road. Give us directions from the nearest highway intersection or a GPS pin dropped on the actual spot, along with the gate code and whether any dogs will be loose. The first real obstacle is usually the crossover from the road. Most rural roads have table drains either side, and the driveway crosses the drain on a culvert pipe with fill over it. Some of those crossovers were built for a car and a horse float, not a loaded rigid truck, and the edges crumble when a heavy wheel goes near them. Tell us how wide your crossover is and whether the edges are solid. After that comes the drive itself: often long, gravel, curving between trees, with low branches and sometimes an overhead line running to the pump shed or the house. Power lines and branches set the height limit for a tilt-tray, which lifts the container well above the truck deck as it slides off. Finally there is the drop spot. A tilt-tray needs a straight, firm run to it and room to drive away afterwards, and on a block with a lot of trees that is not always where you first imagined. Through the wet, the soft parts of any block get softer, and a truck needs firm ground all the way in and out. Photos from the road, along the drive and at the spot answer nearly every question in advance.

sections.h: The crossover, the drive and the gate
p: Most rural deliveries that go wrong do so within the first fifty metres. The culvert crossover at the road is the usual culprit, because its edges hide how narrow it is and a loaded truck turning in needs more width than a car. The gate is the second: measure the gap between the posts, not the width of the gate itself, and note whether anything sticks out, such as a letterbox, a mailbox post or a hinge. If the gate is locked or coded, tell us how to open it. If dogs will be on the block, lock them up before the truck arrives, because a driver guiding a container down off a tilt-tray cannot also watch for a dog. Think about where the container will sit in relation to the bore, the septic system and any buried water or power lines, too. A loaded truck driving over a septic tank or a shallow pipe can break it, and the owner is usually the only one who knows where those are. Mark them with a stake or a bit of flagging tape before the truck arrives.

Plenty of rural owners work in town and cannot be home for a delivery. That is fine, provided the details are settled beforehand. We need a phone number that will be answered on the day, a photo of the exact spot with something marking it, and the gate arrangements. A neighbour who can meet the driver is even better. If the spot is not ready, or the ground has gone soft after a storm, it is better to ring and move the booking than to leave a truck to guess. Our Darwin stock sits a short run away, so moving a date is not the end of the world.

sections.h: Mango season and the farm calendar
p: Mangoes shape the rural area's year. Flowering, spraying and then harvest bring pickers, bins and packing crews onto the orchards, and the packing sheds and access roads are at their busiest while the fruit is coming off. A container delivery in the middle of that is an interruption nobody on a farm wants. Aim to have it in before harvest, or once the last fruit has gone to market, and put it somewhere that will not be in the way of bins and trucks next season. Growers use containers for cartons, trays, packaging and equipment, and those need to stay dry and clean, so ventilation and a well-sealed door matter more than they might in a shed.

Farm chemicals are a separate question. Sprays and fertilisers come with their own rules on bunding, airflow and signage, and a plain dry-freight unit does not satisfy those simply because it locks. Check what applies to your operation before deciding that a container is the answer, and if it is, ask about a unit built for dangerous goods. The same thinking applies to fuel for pumps and machinery: keep only what you need, store it upright, and keep it away from ignition sources.

Horse properties and hobby farms have calmer calendars but similar needs. Feed, tack, rugs and saddles go mouldy quickly in the wet if a container is sealed up with no airflow, and rodents will find a gap in a door seal if there is grain inside. Vents, pallets, sealed feed bins and a quick check of the door rubbers before each wet season keep a container useful for years. Place it where you can reach it with a ute and a trailer in all weathers, not just where it looks tidy in the dry.

sections.h: Fire season, gamba grass and the ground around the box
p: Late in the dry season the rural area burns. Grass that grew head-high through the wet dries out, and gamba grass in particular grows tall and dense and burns very hot. Rural blocks in Litchfield are expected to keep firebreaks, and the area around a container deserves the same care. Keep the grass slashed around it, do not stack timber, fuel or rubbish against it, and do not put it where a fire front would run straight into it. A steel container is not protection from a grass fire. The steel gets extremely hot, and anything inside can be damaged or lost. Treat it as secure storage and keep the ground around it clean.

The same planning helps with the wet that follows. Put the container on the higher, firmer part of the block, clear of the low ground where water lies after heavy rain, and on pads so the floor sits off the ground. The roof sheds rain, yet sheet water crossing a paddock will creep under the doors, and a unit with nothing inside it can be lifted and carried off by a flood. Whether a container that stays on the block needs a permit or an engineered tie-down is a question for Litchfield Council and a building certifier. Give 1300 467 776 a ring with the lot and road name and what the box is for, and the rural cartage is built into the one price.

faqs.q: My block is on a gravel road off the Arnhem Highway. Can a truck get in?
faqs.a: Most of the time, yes. What decides it is the crossover over the table drain, the gate width, the drive and the drop spot. Measure the gap between the gate posts, check whether the crossover edges are solid, and note any low branches or power lines along the drive. Send photos from the road, along the drive and at the spot. Through the wet, the answer can change after a heavy storm, so we may suggest waiting for the ground to firm up.

faqs.q: Can you deliver if nobody is home?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as everything is arranged beforehand. We need a phone number that will be answered on the day, the gate code or key arrangements, dogs secured, and a clear photo of the exact spot with something marking it. A neighbour who can meet the driver is even better. If the spot turns out to be unsuitable on the day, the driver will ring rather than guess.

faqs.q: Do you deliver to Berry Springs and Batchelor?
faqs.a: Yes. Berry Springs, Darwin River and the rest of the Litchfield rural area are all covered, and Batchelor is further down the Stuart Highway toward Litchfield National Park. Council rules differ: Humpty Doo, Howard Springs and Berry Springs are in the Litchfield Council area, while Batchelor is in the Coomalie council area. Check with the right one for your block before ordering.

faqs.q: Can I store mango cartons and packing gear in a container?
faqs.a: Yes, and many growers do. Keep cartons and packaging dry and clean with vents at both ends, pallets under the stacks, and a door that seals properly. Ask for a cargo-worthy or new single-trip unit, because those grades are sold wind and watertight, while as-is units are not. Keep farm chemicals out of that container: storing sprays properly has its own requirements.

faqs.q: Can you get a container out to a fishing camp toward the Mary River?
faqs.a: In the dry season, usually yes, if the track to the camp suits a loaded truck. East along the Arnhem Highway the country drops onto the Adelaide River and Mary River floodplains, and low sections of road and tracks can go under after heavy rain, so wet season deliveries out there are often not possible. Tell us the location, the track surface and whether there is anything on site to help unload, and we will tell you what is realistic. Plan these for the dry.
